analysis.investment_thesis: Oswal Pumps has extraordinary underlying economics — EBIT CAGR of 120%+ and a capital-light model generating triple-digit ROIC on pre-IPO operating capital — but the Magic Formula earnings yield (~11% on EV of ~₹3,800 Cr) falls just shy of my 12% buy threshold. A catastrophic 2025 OCF of −₹151 Cr against ₹281 Cr net profit destroys the "real earnings" case, making this a watch-and-wait at current prices.
key_strengths: Exceptional ROIC on operating capital: stripping out ~₹1,200 Cr IPO cash from invested capital yields ROIC well above 50% — the underlying business is extremely capital-light
Margin expansion is real: operating margin expanded from 10.8% (2022) → 15.1% → 20.2% → 29.4% (2025) as revenue scaled 4× to ₹1,430 Cr
PM-KUSUM structural tailwind: government solar pump subsidies create a durable demand runway with near-zero competition risk from traditional pump makers
key_risks: Negative FCF is disqualifying: 2025 OCF = −₹151 Cr vs. net profit of ₹281 Cr — a ₹432 Cr working capital drain signals government receivable buildup, a classic Indian infra trap
IPO-inflated equity base (₹44 Cr → ₹1,497 Cr in 3 years) means future ROIC will compress sharply; deploying ₹1,200+ Cr of IPO proceeds at similar returns is unlikely
Earnings yield at 8.3–11% (depending on cash treatment) is below my 12% buy threshold — the market has already priced in significant growth
red_flags: 2025 Free Cash Flow: −₹198 Cr — company is cash-flow negative despite 25.8% operating margins, almost certainly due to government subsidy receivables aging on the balance sheet
Finance costs grew 73.8% CAGR (₹8 Cr → ₹42 Cr) despite D/E of only 0.08 — inconsistency suggests off-balance-sheet financing or working capital debt not fully captured
Net profit CAGR of 154.7% with near-zero cash conversion screams aggressive revenue recognition risk — I need 3+ years of positive FCF before trusting these earnings
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula math: EBIT 2025 = ₹420 Cr. If I accept the EV/EBITDA of 8.85× (implying EV ≈ ₹3,832 Cr, meaning ~₹1,222 Cr cash on balance sheet post-IPO), then Earnings Yield = 420/3,832 = 11% — right at the border of attractive but below my 12% threshold. On operating capital excluding IPO cash (≈₹400 Cr invested), ROIC is stratospheric at 100%+, confirming the underlying business is genuinely exceptional. The solar pump model benefits from recurring government procurement, low capex (₹25 Cr/year pre-IPO), and the dominant Oswal brand in Haryana/Punjab agricultural belt. This is a legitimately good business.

The problem is cash flow. In 2025, despite ₹420 Cr EBIT and ₹281 Cr net profit, the company burned ₹151 Cr of operating cash and ₹198 Cr of free cash flow. Government solar scheme receivables in India can age 12–18 months, and the company likely has massive PM-KUSUM receivables sitting uncollected. Until OCF turns positive and FCF conversion reaches ≥60% of net profit, reported earnings cannot be trusted for Magic Formula purposes. At 14× trailing P/E the stock isn't expensive for the growth rate, but Greenblatt's formula requires real, cash-backed earnings — these aren't there yet.
